dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: The accuracy still isn't where it needs to be... We're going to need some time before we can call it a day with the improvements.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Accuracy?

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Well... To be more specific, it comes down to two of our core capabilities...

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Whether it's the accuracy of our long-range target identification or of our muskets, field artillery, and crossbows, there's still room for improvement.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Improving these two metrics will give us a clear advantage on the battlefield, as it will provide more reaction time and increase our effective range.

choices.text: But what if you can't stop the enemy with just long-range warfare?

response.speaker: Leonore
response.text: Then it's time to draw your sword, raise your shield, and settle it with some good old-fashioned face-to-face combat.

response.speaker: Leonore
response.text: Unlike our friends over at the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol in Fontaine, the Knights of Favonius are required to master swordsmanship before they can move on to other weapons.

response.speaker: Leonore
response.text: Even the knights of Ranged Company, which primarily trains with muskets, have to complete the swordsmanship requirement in their annual evaluations.

response.speaker: Leonore
response.text: They have to demonstrate the ability to land a solid hit on a Hilichurl Fighter within three moves, as that'd buy them some time before help from other knights arrives.

response.speaker: Leonore
response.text: The standards are even higher for those in Combined Arms Company.

response.speaker: Leonore
response.text: In short, the training objective is crystal clear: whether the enemy fights us from a distance or gets up close, we make sure that it doesn't end well for them!

choices.text: Or what if the enemy manages to close in on you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There will definitely be something else to work on once this job is done.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Good point. You certainly have it all figured out.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: That's why I need to draw a clear line for myself. One last job, and then I'm out!

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: I'm heading straight to Captain Frederica's office to request my discharge as soon as I finalize the Signal Officer manual with Phonia!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're...

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: As you can see, I'm just an ordinary windmill technician...

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Haha, just kidding. Who knows, we might just have the chance to fight together someday, Honorary Knight.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: I am Leonore, Combined Arms Company's Signals Officer. I've got a few years before retirement, so I'm still useful for now.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Of course, the person you'll be working with will probably be my trainee, Eija Gretel. She's shadowing Amber right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your trainee... is shadowing Amber?

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Yes, a Signals Officer's core mission is reconnaissance, and Amber has far more experience in this than any of us.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: But of course, there is a difference between going on a solo recon mission and leading a scouting party from the front.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: But when it comes to plotting routes, picking positions, and staying undetected, there's a lot Amber can teach Eija!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I shan't keep you any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Leonore
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it... Well, goodbye for now.
